title: George Gershwin's birth chart
metaDescription: George Gershwin's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 3.6° Libra. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Five of the ten placements whose signs are settled fall in air signs — at least half of what the unknown hour leaves certain. Air signs carry exchange in the scheme — comparison, argument, the sentence that makes the situation legible.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Libra, but precisely: 3.6°, first decan, 0°–10°, under Venus in the triplicity scheme. The tradition kept these divisions because thirty degrees is a long street.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Virgo (17.1°), Venus in Scorpio (20.0°), Mars in Cancer (13.8°): a mind that trusts the measured and the checked, taste tuned to mood and undertow, drive that moves on certainty and current.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Jupiter to Pluto is the closest call of the day, a trine within 1.2°. Trines are read as inheritance rather than achievement: the ease is genuine, and nothing about it was earned. Behind it, Mercury square Pluto at 1.4°, and Mercury sextile Venus at 2.8° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: Neptune stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Of the seven planets the classical scheme judges, four sit in a sign it has an opinion about. The Sun in Libra at 3.6° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Mercury in Virgo at 17.1° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Venus in Scorpio at 20.0° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Mars in Cancer at 13.8° is in fall. Condition, not character: that is all the dignity table ever measured.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Counting only the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the chart runs 5 air, 2 water, 2 fire, 1 earth by element and 5 mutable, 3 cardinal, 2 fixed by modality. Pluto was retrograde — motion that reverses only from this vantage point, and which the old reading treats as delay used for revision.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Aquarius for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 14.2° between midnight and midnight. Fast enough that its degree is approximate, slow enough that its sign is not in doubt. At the noon reference it stands at 21.1°.
